item.title: Bulk mesophases modeling of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Aditya Vats, Alenka Mertelj, Miha Ravnik
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78039-1 Ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals are an emerging class of materials in which nematic orientational order coexists with spontaneous macroscopic polarization. Vats et al. develop a free-energy framework to rationalize their bulk structures and predict potential bend-instability-driven mesophases.

item.title: Scientists discover first type I superconductor that breaks time-reversal symmetry
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with no resistance and expel magnetic fields when cooled to ultralow temperatures. And depending on their quantum structure, they can also showcase strange properties like magnetic levitation. But now things are getting a little weirder.

item.title: Cooper pairs found above superconducting critical temperature in pair density waves
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Physicists with the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign's Grainger College of Engineering have identified a new form of superconducting behavior. Experiments on the metal uranium ditelluride reveal that Cooper pairs, the composite electron units responsible for superconductivity, can organize into nonuniform patterns that exist even when the main superconducting phase is absent.

item.title: Q&A: How will quantum computers change society?
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Once called a "pipe dream," quantum computers are now approaching practical use. Companies and research institutes around the world are in fierce competition to develop this technology, which has the potential to rapidly perform some calculations that are extremely difficult even for conventional supercomputers.

item.title: Sustainability cost of defect engineering in color centers for quantum communications
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Sahar Shata, Julie M. Schoenung
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78261-x Sustainable manufacturing is becoming an increasingly important consideration for emerging quantum technologies. Here, the authors assess the environmental, chemical, human-health, and economic impacts of defect engineering strategies for color-center platforms used in quantum communications, highlighting trade-offs between quantum functionality and resource demands while identifying lower-impact solutions.

item.title: Volitional control of wearable robots
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Massimo Sartori, Gregory S. Sawicki
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78416-w This Comment motivates the development of human–machine interfaces that decode spinal motor neuron activity and resulting muscle force information in moving humans. Such interfaces could enable users across the neuromuscular functional spectrum to volitionally control wearable robots with muscle-like behaviour.
